subject: ACME: SLO/SLA measurement and exclusions - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: ACME: SLO/SLA measurement and exclusions - follow-up

Thanks again for today's call — great to meet the team. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a clean draft SLA and mutual action plan over to procurement by early next week.

Recap (from our notes):
- Latency targets you asked for: p95 <= 300ms for non-streaming text generation (single-turn requests).
- Streaming: first-byte (initial token) target <= 500ms; tail latency (complete response) p95 <= 1.2s for typical 256-token responses.
- Throughput/concurrency: target sustained 200 qps with burst up to 500 qps during peak spikes.
- Concurrency is measured as simultaneous inflight requests to the inference pool.
- Workload: median request size ~120 tokens, 99th ~800 tokens; some multimodel routing (embedding + generation) in pipeline.

Open questions (we need your confirmation on these to align SLO language):
1) Do you want SLAs based on server-side processing only (Redwood ingress->egress), or end-to-end observed from your client (includes network)?
2) Should we include separate SLOs for streaming first-byte vs. complete-response?
3) Any required exclusions aside from scheduled maintenance (e.g., customer-side network, third-party provider incidents)?
4) Reporting cadence: weekly dashboard + monthly SLA report acceptable?

Next steps:
- Please confirm the open questions and the concurrency/throughput numbers.
- I attached a mutual action plan (stub) and a draft SLA clause — Rafael and Dev will review internal feasibility and confirm any limits/caps on remedies.

If you confirm, I’ll send a clean SLA draft and the DocuSign link for initial signoff.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME-Mutual-Action-Plan.pdf

From: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: "ACME Platform" <platform@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: SLO/SLA measurement and exclusions - follow-up

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side:

- Measurement: we strongly prefer SLA measurement to be "end-to-end observed" from our application layer (client observed) where possible. However, we understand Redwood measures server-side. Can you confirm the difference and whether you can provide both server-side and client-observed metrics?
- Streaming: yes, we want first-byte SLOs separate from complete-response SLOs. First-byte is particularly important for UX.
- Exclusions: in addition to scheduled maintenance, please exclude incidents caused by our misconfiguration (e.g., bad request patterns) and third-party cloud provider outages — but we need transparency of root cause analysis so we can accept those exclusions.
- Reporting cadence: weekly dashboard is fine, but we also need SLA violations reported within 24 hours of detection and a monthly aggregated report for exec review.

One more: what is your proposed remedy structure for SLA breaches (credit % tiers, cap, and calculation method)? Our procurement team will evaluate.

If you can confirm the measurement details and send a draft SLA clause that includes reporting cadence and remedy examples, we can circulate internally.

—Sam
Sam Lee
Head of Platform Engineering | ACME Solutions
sam.lee@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: SLO/SLA measurement and exclusions - follow-up

Thanks Sam — great questions. Below is how Redwood measures and how we suggest the SLA language be framed. Rafael / Dev, please flag if any of the feasibility/cap numbers need adjustment.

Measurement (recommended):
- Primary SLA (server-side): measured from time request is accepted by Redwood ingress to time final token is emitted by the model runtime (server-side processing). This excludes last-mile network latency on either side.
- Optional client-observed metrics: we can provide synthetic/observed metrics measured from a small set of customer-controlled probes deployed in your region. These are provided for transparency but are not the primary SLA metric (they can be used in operational runbooks).

Streaming specifics:
- First-byte latency: measure time from Redwood ingress to first token emitted (p95 <= 500ms in our proposal).
- Tail/complete-response latency: measure time until final token emitted (p95 <= 1.2s for 256-token typical response).

Exclusions (suggested list to include in SLA):
- Scheduled maintenance windows (with at least 48 hours notice).
- Force majeure (as defined in the master services agreement).
- Third-party provider outage affecting Redwood's network or compute layer (we will provide RCA).
- Customer-originated misconfiguration or abusive traffic patterns that materially degrade service (we will engage customer prior to applying exclusion).

Reporting cadence and escalation:
- Real-time dashboards in Console (shared access) with rolling p50/p95/p99.
- Automated weekly summary emailed to your ops inbox.
- SLA violation alerting: violations detected by our monitoring will generate a ticket and an automated alert; for confirmed SLA breaches, we commit to notifying within 24 hours with an initial summary, and a full RCA within 7 business days.

Remedies (proposal):
- Credit tiers based on severity: 5% monthly invoice credit for a single confirmed SLA violation window; 10% for repeated material violations in a month.
- Cap: cumulative credits for SLA breaches limited to 30% of a single monthly invoice.
- Calculation: credits pro-rated based on the percentage of requests in the impacted window failing the SLO compared to baseline.

Next steps:
- I’ve attached a short draft of SLA clauses that reflect the above. Rafael and Dev: can you confirm that the proposed metrics (p95 numbers, first-byte measurement, 200 qps sustained / 500 qps burst) are operationally supportable given our current Dedicated sizing and fallback rules?
- Sam: if that looks broadly acceptable we’ll push a slightly cleaned-up doc to DocuSign and include the mutual action plan timeline.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-draft-sla-clauses.docx

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME: SLO/SLA measurement and exclusions - follow-up

Short internal check — we can support the proposed SLOs with these caveats:
- p95 = 300ms for non-streaming is OK on dedicated pools for typical 120-token median if they accept ~30% quantized model profile; for 800-token tails we should set separate p95 targets or bump Dedicated capacity.
- Streaming first-byte p95 <= 500ms is reasonable if we reserve a fractional slot for low-latency routing (adds minimal cost).
- Remedy cap at 30% monthly is standard; procurement may push back but it's realistic.

I’ll follow up with a short note on model-variant fallback language for the SLA (to clarify when we route to a higher-latency but compatible model).

—Rafael
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
